name: com.mckrill.avbd
description: GPU-resident Augmented Vertex Block Descent (AVBD) physics for Unity: rigid bodies, joints and soft bodies solved entirely on the GPU and rendered through URP.

samples.description: Runs the CPU reference solver live in a scene: upstream demo scenes, sequential versus colored sweep, graph-color tint, contact and joint overlays.
A pyramid of 140 or more boxes on the GPU solver. Shoot boxes from the camera and adjust their speed, size and mass in the panel. Needs the contact stages in AvbdSolver.Step().

A brick wall of 225 or more blocks, on an immobile bottom row, held together by joints that fracture, on the GPU solver. Shoot boxes at it and set the joints' stiffness, the fracture threshold and the blocks' density in the panel.

The fracture wall made of spheres instead of bricks: 225 or more spheres in a hexagonal packing, on an immobile bottom row, held together by joints that fracture, on the GPU solver. Shoot cubes at it and set the joints' stiffness, the fracture threshold and the spheres' density in the panel.
The 110 440-brick ring of the performance test: 40 courses of bricks in running bond, hit by a cube, on the GPU solver. Shoot boxes at it, resize it, and switch the order the bodies are stored in.

Spawns the objects of a list of voxel files (JSON made from an STL mesh by Tools/Voxelize/voxelize_stl.py), 5 m apart: every voxel is a box and neighboring voxels are linked by fracturing ball-socket joints. Shoot boxes at them or blow them up.

The 34 880-voxel, 241 872-joint scene of the performance test Scenario6_VoxelImpact35k: two cubes, two spheres and two toruses made of fracturing voxels collide head-on at 50 m/s. Shoot boxes at them, change the speed and the joint settings.
